ruling: guard-comments keeps the 3-changed-text-line paragraph detector, but a paragraph blocks only the first time it is shown. Each sighting is an empty file named <anchor>.<30-day window> under <git-common-dir>/devkit/comment-shown/, which ship worktrees share; the anchor is the file plus surrounding code. The block is printed before its sighting is recorded, so an interrupted run never passes a paragraph unseen. Files are created exclusively and never rewritten or deleted, so concurrent gates cannot erase each other's sightings, and a sighting older than 30 days no longer counts. A later attempt that keeps or rewords the paragraph passes and counts as kept. devkit review never touches the store, so it reports every finding. A store that cannot be read or written exits 4. The remedy follows Bun Comment Cop: shorten where possible; a paragraph that justifies a workaround means the code is wrong, so fix the code; if every line states something the code cannot, retry unchanged. A second, opt-in rule blocks on every attempt: guard.config.json comments.forbiddenRefs (regular expressions) and comments.forbidDecisionRefs (the decisionsDir path and hyphenated decision record names from the commit index, matched as whole words) are matched against added lines of every comment token. A removed comment fragment in the same change run, read from HEAD by the lexer and identical up to whitespace, excuses one added fragment, so a code-only edit keeps its trailing reference while a reworded, shortened, swapped or pasted one blocks. Both reference keys default off; devkit sets them. comment_budget gains kept and refs counts.
